rationale: The candidate reads as one compact dominant mass in all four views, so it is not visually fragmented or view-dependent. However, the form remains largely a generalized swollen prism with only a small local cut on one side; the access edge is not convincingly answered by an active public threshold, court, or undercut. The parcel response is weak: the mass sits inside the boundary but does not clearly organize an open-space figure or orientation around the site edge. Programmatically, neighborhood living wants an active ground condition and a clear public void/terrace; this object looks more like an introverted sculpted block than a mixed-use street building. The geometry is coherent enough to avoid repair collapse, but the section logic does not yet carry the required public-ground relation. The strongest transferable move is to preserve the dominant bar-like anchor and introduce a more deliberate carved court/notch aligned to the access side.
